en.title: Tokyo stays: Shinagawa, Osaki, Gotanda
en.cardDesc: Three spots on the Yamanote Line, each with a different neighborhood feel.
en.html:
Tokyo stays: Shinagawa, Osaki, Gotanda

Source: Merry Journey

Shinagawa（品川）

The easiest station for Haneda — Keikyu takes about 15–20 minutes. Stay at 品川王子大飯店 — about two minutes from the station, Tokyo Tower from the high floors, pool / bowling / cinema on site.

Next door is Maxell Aqua Park, a compact aquarium with dolphin shows (the first four rows get splashed).

Osaki（大崎）

One stop down the Yamanote, plus the Rinkai Line straight to Odaiba — more of a lived-in Tokyo feel. New Otani Inn Tokyo connects to the station under cover, with rooms wider than a typical business hotel. Behind it, OAKI New City has a large supermarket (wagyu, prepared food), Daiso, and plenty to eat.

Gotanda（五反田）

Transfer to the Toei Asakusa Line for Skytree, Ginza, Nihonbashi; some trains run through to Narita. 東急 Stay 五反田 is under 10 seconds from exit A6, with a washer and microwave — useful for longer stays. A one-minute walk to a five-floor Don Quijote.

en.title: Five beef noodle shops in Hsinchu
en.cardDesc: One bowl each at Chenghuang Temple, NTHU, Guangfu Road, Zhongzheng Road, and Zhubei — the map is what shows the distance.
en.html:
Five beef noodle shops in Hsinchu

Hsinchu beef noodle is not one street competing with itself — it is five points. Chenghuang Temple, NTHU, Guangfu Road, Zhongzheng Road, and Zhubei each get a bowl; the map is what shows the distance. All five were still open in 2026. Hours and closing days follow the shops; no prices here.

九添福牛肉麵館

九添福牛肉麵館 is at No. 436, Xida Road, North District, a few minutes' walk from 城隍廟. Still on the 2026 Bib Gourmand list. Both red-braised and clear broth; generous meat. Parking around the temple is hard — treat the shop as the pin.

璽子牛肉麵

璽子牛肉麵 main shop is at No. 31, Bo'ai Street, East District, on the municipal zoo / NTHU side. Clear broth, tendon with bite. The jinbing often sells out. Closed Tuesdays; lunch and dinner only. Zhubei and Xiangshan have branches; this piece pins the main shop.

成都老鍋牛肉麵

成都老鍋牛肉麵 is at No. 126, Sec. 2, Guangfu Road, East District — the Hsinchu Science Park / NTHU after-work axis. Sichuan-leaning but not pure heat; the bone broth cooks longer. Closed Wednesdays. Same stretch as 璽子 on Bo'ai Street, but too far to walk as one meal. Treat them as two pins.

臻穎牛肉麵食館

臻穎牛肉麵食館 is at No. 366, Zhongzheng Road, near the Air Force Hospital and Big City. Moved from Minsheng Road in 2025. Thirty-plus years of juancun taste. The Five Blessings bowl puts tendon, tendon core, pork belly, tripe, and tendon in one bowl. Closed Mondays; cars are hard to park nearby.

文化城牛肉麵

文化城牛肉麵 jumps to No. 486, Guangming 1st Road, Zhubei — not the same map scale as the four in the city. Large cuts, many small plates; iced tea refills for dine-in. Closed Thursdays. The pig's trotter often sells out; come early if you want it on the side.

Do not try all five in one day. Pick one bowl as this visit's anchor, then start the next from the other side of the map.

en.title: Yangmingshan: one night, two days on foot
en.cardDesc: Tienlai as the base. Qixing from Xiaoyoukeng; the fish trail uphill the next day.
en.html:
Yangmingshan: one night, two days on foot

Split a holiday from a workout and the weekend becomes two jobs: one day sleeping in the car, one day forcing a climb. This time we flipped it — book 陽明山天籟渡假酒店 as the base, climb 七星山 on Saturday, and on Sunday climb the fish trail from 上磺溪 toward 擎天崗, both days from the same bed.

Why Tienlai

This is the seaward side of Yangmingshan, not the Beitou strip. 天籟 is in Jinshan. After enough Qixing sulfur on the mountain, the nose is already dull in the lobby. The lower end of the north fish trail is on this side — Sunday you can start at the foot and climb up, then back to the bed, without stuffing yourself back into the city. Soak the legs and stop.

Saturday｜Qixing

Park at 小油坑 and start the climb to 七星山主峰 from there. Short, steep stone steps; fumaroles hiss beside you; sulfur works into the throat. The legs complain before the lungs. Wind on the summit dries the sweat; only wind left in the ears. Below: white smoke and ridgeline, not a view staged for anyone. Sit a while, then the same way down. Legs still shaking back at Tienlai; the water is the temperature that matches the day.

Sunday｜north fish trail, uphill

Day two is not another Qixing. Walk the fish trail — Jinbaoli Road, the old route that carried fish over the mountain. This day we climb: start at 上磺溪, through 憨丙厝地 (you can stop by the stone house and catch your breath — travelers used to mend straw sandals here), then on toward 金包里城門 / Qingtiangang. Uneven stone steps underfoot, shade in stretches; where the soles pick up wet soil, the stride shortens on its own. This day is a climb, not a slide from the gate down toward Xiahuangxi.

We walked it then. Check the notices before you start at Shanghuangxi; if it is closed, do not treat this route as current.

Map order: Tienlai → Xiaoyoukeng / Qixing → Shanghuangxi → Hanbingcuodi → the gate (uphill) → back to Tienlai. Two days, one sleeping coordinate.

Still to write: other north-Taiwan “one night + two days on foot,” bikes, the coast, living-water lake days off — pin those next. First piece in the resort-fitness series.

en.title: Tokyo tabletop market: how to stay in Makuhari, which day to recover (Autumn 2026)
en.cardDesc: Pin the bed and recovery first; after two hall days, leave another day for the legs.
en.html:
Tokyo tabletop market: how to stay in Makuhari, which day to recover (Autumn 2026)

Not gone yet. For October I want to park a holiday on Tokyo's tabletop-game market — Japanese usually writes ゲームマーケット / Game Market. Not a video-game expo: you playtest and buy new titles. Both days are standing playtests; the bag only gets heavier. What I want clear is how close the bed is to the hall, and which day I soak the legs or take the sea wind.

Makuhari — do not commute from Shinjuku

幕張メッセ sits against 海浜幕張. The picture I want: bags back in the room, then into the hall empty-handed. If the fair means a Shinjuku run every night, the legs will fail before the wallet. 2026/10/17–18; details on gamemarket.jp. Booth maps are only accurate at the door; this piece does not draw them.

Check in first

Find a bed on the Kaihin-Makuhari side. 10/16 can be the arrival: land in Tokyo, check in, deal with jet lag and luggage, then walk in Saturday and Sunday. Shop names wait until that year's rooms; do not sleep cheap an hour away.

Two days in the hall, leave another day for the legs

The hall is only Saturday and Sunday. The trip can be: one day land and check in, two days playtesting inside メッセ, then a full day off the floor, last day home. That day is not for packing in sights — the legs already stood two days; stuffing an outlet or a city tour only makes them worse the next morning. Better the waterfront, a soak, or staying in the room, so the legs can come back.

Sea wind

幕張海浜公園. When the hall lights and voices are still in the ears, go look at the horizon. Walk a loop or ride a short stretch; stop when the wind is enough.

Hot water

幕張温泉 湯楽の里 is more on-target than a mall. After two days standing, what you want is to get in the water. Over by JFA Yume Field; how to get there and how much, check the official site before you go.

One dinner outside the hall is enough, around the station. Three things on the map: メッセ, a bed you can get back to, the park or the bath. Tickets and hours follow the official site.

en.title: A walking elephant in the Nantes shipyard
en.cardDesc: Not been yet. The mechanical elephant, the river rings, the grey crane.
en.html:
A walking elephant in the Nantes shipyard

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there. Nantes sits on the west of France, toward the Atlantic; the high-speed train from Paris is a little over two hours. On the river island an old shipyard became a mechanical-art park — not a zoo. I want to go for the mechanical elephant that lifts its legs and walks: Les Machines de l'Île (Machines of the Isle of Nantes). Check the downtime calendar before you leave.

Les Machines de l'Île

The park is at the west end of Île de Nantes, in the Loire, at Parc des Chantiers. The headline is the Grand Éléphant: about twelve metres high, about forty-eight tonnes, wood and steel, ears that move, a trunk that mists water, walking slowly through the park. Standing in the park you can watch it pass for free; a Voyage ticket is what lets you climb on for about thirty minutes, around forty or fifty people at a time, and from the back you can see how the joints lift the legs. Departures are limited; in high season you usually book online first.

What the elephant walks on

Electricity — battery / hybrid traction; the legs and joints are lifted mainly by hydraulics and pneumatics, not petrol. It walks slowly. After the 2018 hybrid change it is quieter. A driver steers. Details: lesmachines-nantes.fr／Grand Éléphant.

The gallery and the marine carousel

The other two blocks are separate tickets. Galerie des Machines is a living machine hall: spiders, insects, birds and other large mechanical creatures, about an hour, with operators who talk and make the machines move. Carrousel des Mondes Marins (Marine Worlds Carousel) is a three-storey sea carousel, about forty-five minutes; every level has sit-on, moving marine machines — not the little wooden horses of a fairground. The park itself is free to walk. The heron tree they used to advertise (Arbre aux Hérons) was cancelled; only prototype branches remain on site, so do not expect the whole tree from old posters.

When you cannot ride the elephant

The Grand Éléphant does no Voyage from 2026/11/2–2027/2/28 (follow lesmachines-nantes.fr/horaires). The Machines stay open in that window; only the elephant ride is crossed out. The marine carousel has a separate maintenance window 2026/9/21–25; check the same page again before you go.

West along the river

After the Machines I still want to walk west along the river to Quai des Antilles. Les Anneaux is a string of rings standing on the bank; at dusk you want to walk around them. Hangar à Bananes sits on the quay; further on is the grey Grue Titan grise — do not mix it up with the yellow crane inside the park. The north-bank Mémorial de l'abolition is across a bridge, not a few more steps along the same shore.

How other people wrote it

These are other people's trip notes / reports online, not a record of my being there — only for the picture. Do not treat old ticket prices and timetables as current; follow the official site: Room7B01〈Les Machines〉 (Traditional Chinese, on-site detail); RFI〈南特機械島〉 (Traditional Chinese; 2016, atmosphere only); One Small Bag (English, elephant / Galerie / carousel written separately); Petit Futé visit (French).

The picture I want: the west coast of France, shipyard ground, a twelve-metre mechanical elephant, the gallery and a three-level marine carousel, rings and a grey crane on the riverbank. Tickets, downtime, bridges and trams — check the official site again before you go.

en.title: Fulong: one night, bike Old Caoling
en.cardDesc: Want to go. Overnight at Fullon, bike Old Caoling; soak at the beach.
en.html:
Fulong: one night, bike Old Caoling

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there. The Yangmingshan piece pinned holiday and workout to the same bed, and said bikes and the coast were still to write. This time I want to park the holiday in Fulong — book 福容 for one night, then the next day pick up a bike at 福隆車站 and ride into 舊草嶺隧道, both days starting from the same sandspit.

Why Fullon

福容大飯店福隆 sits against the 浴場 and the sandspit — the overnight pole on this map. After the ride or the swim, what you want is to walk back to the room and soak the legs in the ocean hot spring, not drive back into the city. Check fullon-hotels before you go.

The station as hub

福隆車站 is where the bento and the station-front bike rentals sit on top of each other. Bikes leave from here; the tunnel starts counting from here. The pin is approximate — check the rental stall again when you arrive.

Old Caoling: north mouth to south mouth

The ride I want is Old Caoling, not a highway loop. The 北口 is on the Fulong side; the tourism bureau writes 制天險. The 南口 is the Shicheng end, 白雲飛處. Cool inside the tunnel; turn around after the south mouth. The south-mouth pin is a track approximation, not a single official page.

River inside, sea outside

福隆遊客中心 and the 海水浴場 sit on the same side: inner river, outer sea, sand for a swim. The sea-swim season is about 5/1–10/20, lifeguards until 17:00. Details on the Fullon beach page.

Short ridge to the west

I still want to walk west along the sand to 龍門吊橋 — the stretch that joins Longmen to Yanliao. Short, windy. Not the main line; the edge after the tunnel.

Map order: Fullon → station / rental → north mouth → south mouth (and back) → visitor centre / beach → Longmen Bridge → back to Fullon. Two days, one sleeping coordinate.

Resort-fitness series: after two days on foot in Yangmingshan, this piece is the bike and the coast. Still to write: a living-water lake day off — pin that next.

en.title: Akiyoshido: seventeen degrees underground, elevator up to the plateau
en.cardDesc: Not been yet. Seventeen degrees underground, Hundred Dishes, Golden Pillar, elevator to the plateau.
en.html:
Akiyoshido: seventeen degrees underground, elevator up to the plateau

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there. Akiyoshido（あきよしどう） sits on the west of Honshu, in Yamaguchi — about a hundred metres under Mine City's Akiyoshidai Quasi-National Park, a national natural monument. Official pages often say one of the largest; the cave system is Japan's second-longest. I want to go to walk the underground at about seventeen degrees first, then take the elevator up onto the limestone plateau and match the formations to the surface: 秋芳洞正面入口. Do not stuff Shimonoseki, Motonosumi, and Hagi into the same day.

In through the main entrance

The tourist main line starts at the front entrance, about one paved kilometre; the cave stays about seventeen degrees year-round, damp and slippery — trainers and a light jacket. On the way you pass 百枚皿 (travertine terraces stacked like rice paddies) and 黃金柱（黄金柱）. Exact spots inside the cave only line up once you are in; this map starts from the front entrance. From April 2026 tickets and the ticket window changed; check the Japanese official site before you leave (the Traditional Chinese page may be old).

The adventure course is not a caving tour

Beside the main line there is an 冒險コース: a little extra money, a rented torch, a side branch of about ten to fifteen minutes; it closes when the water rises. Details on the official site. This is not a caving tour. If the legs are not enough, just walk the paved kilometre.

Elevator up to the plateau

Midway you can take the elevator to the surface and walk to カルスト展望台 (the limestone-plateau lookout). One ticket lets you re-enter the cave — see the formations below, then grassland and sinkholes above. Choosing the front entrance or the elevator entrance is choosing whether to keep a stretch of energy for the plateau.

How to get there, do not stuff the day

JR Shin-Yamaguchi, then the Bocho Bus to 「秋芳洞」, about forty to forty-five minutes — that is the current main line. The JR Mine Line is still fully suspended; do not treat the train as running. Sections are replacement buses; leave extra time for the connection. By car, get off near Akiyoshidai IC. Taishodo, Shimonoseki / Tsunoshima / Motonosumi, and Hagi / Tsuwano are other days.

The picture I want: west Honshu, seventeen degrees under Mine, Hundred Dishes and the Golden Pillar, an optional torch side-branch, elevator up to the Akiyoshidai grassland. Check karusuto.com／秋芳洞 before you leave.

en.title: Ogose: Kuroyamaen fish-and-grill, three waterfalls on the way
en.cardDesc: Not been yet. Fish and grill at Kuroyamaen, three waterfalls on the same valley road.
en.html:
Ogose: Kuroyamaen fish-and-grill, three waterfalls on the way

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there. Kuroyamaen（くろやまえん） sits in Ogose, Saitama — in the hills west of Tokyo. Ikebukuro, change for Ogose, then into the valley: door to door about an hour and a half to two hours. Kuroyamaen is on the trail toward 黒山三滝 (three waterfalls): you can fish rainbow trout beside the stream, then salt-grill them on charcoal on the spot. The gorge trail at 黒山三滝 is free; if you fish and grill at Kuroyamaen, the rod and the fish are extra. Same valley, two bills. Kuroyamaen has no website of its own — call before you leave to check they are open that day: 049-292-3862.

黒山園

The street address is around Kuroyama 1445, Ogose (a banchi in Japanese addressing). The map pins 黒山園 with an approximate coordinate for this stretch; treat the house number and the site as the truth. A rod plus bait is about 600 yen, two people at most on one rod. A rainbow trout is about 700 yen now; if you still see 600 yen, that is old information — do not treat it as current. This is a managed fishery: fish you catch must be bought before you can grill them or take them home. Paying for the rod alone does not let you walk off with the fish. The grill is usually included in the fish price; grilling takes about thirty to forty minutes, follow the site — that window is enough to walk a few steps toward the falls. Hours disagree across sources, and some days they close without a fixed pattern; the phone is what counts.

黒山三滝（三座瀑布）

The three falls are 男滝, 女滝, and 天狗滝, together 黒山三滝, inside a prefectural nature park. The gorge trail is free year-round; from the 町營停車場 it is about a fifteen-minute walk to the falls. After rain the trail is slick. Kuroyamaen and the three falls sit on the same road, not two far-apart pins — if you want to go, fishing, grilling, and the falls fit in a half day. Further up the valley there are longer mountain routes (for example toward 顔振峠); do not force those onto the same day.

How to get there

Tobu Tojo from Ikebukuro, change to the Tobu Ogose Line to 越生站, then the Kawagoe Kanko bus 「黒山」 into the valley. From April 2026 the bus does not run on weekdays, only Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays, and there are not many trips. On weekdays drive, take a taxi, or leave a long walk. Weekends jam and the car park fills — do not park on the roadside. The same bus also serves a plum grove; that is another sight. Do not stuff it into the same day as Kuroyamaen and 黒山三滝.

The picture I want: a Saitama mountain stream, one rod for two people, charcoal-grill smoke, the sound of three waterfalls. Check the town tourism page again before you leave, and call Kuroyamaen: ogose-kanko.jp／黒山三滝.

en.title: Kawazu: seven waterfalls on the mountain side, the coast another half day
en.cardDesc: Not been yet. Seven waterfalls on the mountain side; the coast is another half day.
en.html:
Kawazu: seven waterfalls on the mountain side, the coast another half day

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there. Kawazu sits on the east coast of the Izu Peninsula. The limited express 「踊り子」 from Tokyo is about two and a half hours; the earliest train only reaches 河津駅 a little after eleven. Stuffing 河津七滝 (seven waterfalls), 天城荘, the geyser, 今井浜, and 舟戸の番屋 into the same day will burst — you will almost never already be standing at the falls at eleven. The want-to-go plan: one day on the mountain side, one day on the coast; if you really join them, use a car or a taxi, and cut the full 七滝 walk.

Mountain side: 七滝 and 天城荘

河津七滝 is a gorge trail — no ticket, no fixed closing day; the full line takes about sixty to ninety minutes, lots of steps, slick after rain.

河津七滝・大滝。Photo: Osumi Akari / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

Near the largest fall is the day-trip outdoor bath at 天城荘: a mixed outdoor pool looking at the waterfall; swimsuits required. Open about ten to sixteen-thirty, last admission sixteen; closed Wednesdays (check again before you leave). Adults 2,000 yen — if you still see 1,000 yen, that is the old price. Bad weather can close it. If you want to go, walking 七滝 then soaking at 天城荘 is enough for the day.

天城荘・大滝旁露天溫泉。Photo: Jpatokal / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

Coast: the geyser, 今井浜, 舟戸

峰温泉大噴湯公園 is a free look at a hot-spring geyser — about nine-thirty to fifteen-thirty, roughly one minute each hour; closed Tuesdays and Fridays for maintenance.

峰温泉大噴湯公園。Photo: Niiryoku2910 / Wikimedia Commons / CC BY-SA 4.0

Next to it you can walk 今井浜; the 2026 sea-bathing season was 25 July to 23 August and is already over — do not expect to swim out of season; walking is fine. Further on, on the fishing-port bluff, is 舟戸の番屋 (the shop name is 「舟戸」, not the often-misspelled 「船戸」): the lookout outdoor bath is about nine to seventeen, last entry sixteen, general ticket 300 yen, closed Tuesdays.

舟戸の番屋。河津町提供／靜岡縣開放資料 / CC BY 4.0（資料頁）

If you really join mountain side and coast

Mountain side to coast is about six to eight kilometres; better drive or take a taxi. A lighter join: morning at 天城荘 (or only the largest fall), then time the geyser on the hour, then 舟戸の番屋; leave the full 七滝 line for another day. Do not run all five pins in one day.

The picture I want: Izu Kawazu, an outdoor bath beside a waterfall, the geyser going off on the hour, a lookout bath toward Sagami Bay. Check 天城荘 and the Kawazu town tourism page again before you leave — hours and closing days change.

en.title: Switzerland: cable cars all the way to the Matterhorn
en.cardDesc: Want to go. From a group-tour trip report on YouTube — Zurich to Milan, cable cars stringing together eight Alpine days.
en.html:
Switzerland: cable cars all the way to the Matterhorn

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there — put together from a group-tour trip report on YouTube. The eight-day route runs on bus transfers and cable cars: luggage doesn't get carried up and down every night, and what a coach tour like this actually saves is legs, for the mountains. Days below are labeled Day 1–8; Bern (Day 4) and Milan (Day 8) are the two dates the video states outright, the rest are inferred from the order things happen in — check the real schedule before you go.

Day 1｜Zurich: the old town first

Land day one, start properly the next. Lindenhof is free, and the old town opens up once you're standing on it. Street fountains are mostly drinkable — save a bottle of water. Grossmünster is under scaffolding outside but open as usual inside, modern stained glass paired with a Charlemagne statue in the crypt. June normally runs 22–23°C; the trip in the video hit a 34°C heatwave — pack short sleeves and sunscreen anyway, weather isn't something you can copy from someone else's packing list.

Day 2｜Grindelwald by cable car, down again into Lucerne

The First cable car is the viewpoint in the Jungfrau region; the top connects to the Cliff Walk and a suspension bridge that sways — anyone afraid of heights should know that going in. Down again and on to Lucerne's Chapel Bridge, one of the oldest wooden bridges left in Europe; eat the cheese pie from the stall by the bridge while it's hot. The Lion Monument is close by, bigger than you'd expect, and the old city-wall viewpoint gives one side lake and one side town in the same frame.

Day 3｜Ferry across Lake Zurich to the city of roses

A two-and-a-half-hour ferry from Zurich to Rapperswil, which puts out about 15,000 roses June through September. The local specialty is pan-fried Egli, no fishy taste at all. The hilltop castle looks out over a wooden bridge the Habsburgs built in the 14th century — about 800 metres, the longest wooden bridge in Switzerland, the water beneath it clear enough to see the birds' feet.

Day 4｜Bern isn't Zurich, and Gruyères is all-you-can-eat

The capital is Bern — the clock tower and the cobbled old town are a World Heritage site, and the city crest is a bear because the founder's first hunt caught one. Locals swim the river to commute in summer. Next is Gruyères: the Cailler chocolate factory nearby in Broc has unlimited tasting, and the village fondue has to use Gruyère cheese, cut with white wine, bread over potato for tasting the cheese properly. The castle was a medieval hunting lodge; the armour and weapons on display show chain mail was the norm before plate armour came along.

Day 5｜Lake Geneva, birthplace of the steak sauce

Chillon Castle stands on Lake Geneva; the inside used to be a dungeon, and the layout is confusing enough that the people in the video lost their own way out. Geneva's old town feels nothing like the modern area around the station — the Broken Chair sculpture and the Flower Clock sit along the lakefront. Dinner is Café de Paris, where the signature herb-butter steak sauce originated.

Day 6｜Chamonix: the weather decides

Chamonix is across in France; the cable car climbs straight to 2,500m for a view of Mont Blanc (literally "white mountain"). You can spot actual hikers walking up from below, next to everyone riding the cable car — a contrast worth noticing. Weather is the biggest variable on this leg; the forecast in the video called for thunderstorms the day before, so if the itinerary can flex, save the clear day for the next stop.

Day 7｜Zermatt: the whole point of the trip

The right side of the Gornergrat railway car is the best seat for the Matterhorn; the observatory looks out on a glacier and several 4,000m peaks at once. A lake along the hiking trail catches the Matterhorn's reflection, and the walk down offers a 20-minute route (more ups and downs) or a 40-minute one (gentler) — fewer people, and the view holds up against what you saw from the train.

Day 8｜Closing out: across into Italy, ending in Milan

First stop after leaving Switzerland is Stresa — prices drop noticeably the moment you cross the border. Orta San Giulio, one of Italy's most beautiful villages, has a short boat ride out to the island in the middle of the lake. The trip closes at Milan's Duomo — no photos allowed inside — and afterward there's the Starbucks built into a former post office, billed as the world's most beautiful.

How other people wrote it

This piece is put together from a YouTube trip report, "First trip to Switzerland! Moved by 8 days of Alpine scenery" — not a record of my being there. Route and details follow the video; check actual duration, weather, and opening hours against official sites before you go.

The picture I want: fountain water in Zurich's old town, the Cliff Walk off First, Chapel Bridge, the roses and long wooden bridge at Rapperswil, the Gruyères fondue, the dungeon at Chillon, Mont Blanc from Chamonix, the Matterhorn's reflection at Zermatt, closing at Milan's Duomo. Map order: Zurich → Grindelwald → Lucerne → Rapperswil → Bern → Gruyères → Geneva → Chamonix → Zermatt → Stresa → Orta San Giulio → Milan.

en.title: Scandinavia: seven days strung together by ferry
en.cardDesc: Want to go. From a group-tour trip report on YouTube — Copenhagen to Stockholm, ferries stringing together seven days across three countries.
en.html:
Scandinavia: seven days strung together by ferry

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there — put together from a group-tour trip report on YouTube. Seven days across Denmark, Norway and Sweden, linked by ferry crossings; the same channel's next trip after this one is Switzerland, so it's a companion piece to that story. Days below follow the order things happen in the video; only Day 1 (Copenhagen) and the final day (Stockholm) are stated outright, the rest are inferred from context — check the real schedule before you go.

Day 1｜Copenhagen: a day to wander before the tour starts

A late flight meant landing the night before, so the first full day is free — the group tour itself starts a day later. Nyhavn, the row of colourful harbour houses, is the city's postcard image: a 17th-century quay once full of sailors. Lunch is smørrebrød, Danish open sandwiches piled with fish, shrimp, or mayonnaise in every combination. Bikes outnumber pedestrians here — Denmark runs on them. The afternoon is Tivoli Gardens, which opened in 1843, over a century before Disneyland — Walt Disney is said to have visited before building his own park — and still has an old-fashioned haunted house, a rare find abroad.

Day 2｜Copenhagen wraps up, on to Odense

The official group tour starts today. The city highlight is Amalienborg Palace and the Little Mermaid statue — easy to forget the fairy tale actually ends with her turning to sea foam. An hour of free time goes to cafés and Danish design shops, where the taste shows even in small everyday objects. In the afternoon the group bus heads to Odense, luggage left on board. This is Hans Christian Andersen's hometown, and the whole town looks like it stepped out of his illustrations — bread by the river, and a lucky catch of a street puppet show retelling one of his stories, charming enough to land even without understanding the dialogue. Dinner is traditional Danish plaice, pan-fried in plenty of butter.

Day 3｜Ferry crossing into Norway

Mostly a ferry day: crossing the Skagerrak Strait from Denmark to Norway on a ship large enough to have a food court and restaurants, no seasickness involved. The Norwegian port on the other side is Stavanger, its old quarter of white wooden houses — and cats wandering everywhere — intact enough to feel like a storybook town.

Day 4｜Bergen: city of rain, city of fjords

The cable car up Fløyen gives a full view over Bergen, a city known both as the rainiest in Norway and the gateway to the fjords — rain more than half the year, and reportedly one inspiration behind the setting of Frozen. Partway up, a monument of oversized swords commemorating Norway's unification is bigger than expected. Down at the fish market, salmon and fish soup are the things to order — the soup tastes like a rich seafood cream stew. The UNESCO-listed Bryggen wharf is a row of narrow wooden buildings leaning on each other for support, once the base for German merchants and now full of Nordic-design shops.

Day 5｜Sognefjord, the trip’s centerpiece

The highlight of the whole itinerary is a cruise on Sognefjord, over 200km long, carved by glaciers and then filled by the sea, cliffs rising steeply on both sides — eating a hot dog on deck with this as the backdrop feels oddly fitting. The hotel that night sits near an unusual building with a stacked, dragon-topped roof built using Viking-era construction methods. The evening ends in Oslo.

Day 6｜Oslo wraps up, on to Sweden

Oslo's centerpiece is Vigeland Sculpture Park, where the central column stacked with human figures represents humanity reaching for the divine — visitors line up to copy the statues' poses for photos. The Munch Museum holds several versions of The Scream; the famous one is the oil painting, but what's usually on display is the pastel or print version, alongside Munch's other well-known work, Madonna. Leaving Oslo for Sweden, the route stops at Örebro, an open-air-museum town that keeps its 19th-century look, cobblestone lanes lined with cafés and shops. The evening reaches Stockholm, the final hotel of the trip.

Day 7｜Stockholm: free day, trip wraps up

The last day is unstructured — the tour officially ends once it's over. Lunch is proper Swedish meatballs with lingonberry sauce, bigger than expected. In the old town, Gamla Stan, the Royal Armoury holds historic weapons and armour, including crossbows once banned for being too powerful. A tram ride out to Djurgården island, home to an aquarium and an amusement park, leads to the real destination: the Vasa Museum, housing a 17th-century warship that sank shortly after launch and survived in astonishingly complete condition — more convincing than any pirate ship in the movies. With time left, the island's garden is a good spot for a closing coffee.

How other people wrote it

This piece is put together from a YouTube trip report, "The best Nordic trip: 7 days through Denmark, the Norwegian fjords, and Sweden" — not a record of my being there. Route and details follow the video; check actual duration, ferry schedules, and opening hours against official sites before you go.

The picture I want: the colourful houses of Nyhavn, the old-fashioned haunted house at Tivoli, the street puppet show in Odense, fish soup at the Bergen market, the wooden warehouses of Bryggen, the Sognefjord cruise, the column at Vigeland Park, the Vasa Museum. Map order: Copenhagen → Odense → Stavanger → Bergen → Sognefjord → Oslo → Örebro → Stockholm.

en.title: Tateyama Murodo: a plateau at two thousand four hundred and fifty metres
en.cardDesc: Not been yet. Murodo-daira at 2,450 m; a short walk around Mikurigaike.
en.html:
Tateyama Murodo: a plateau at two thousand four hundred and fifty metres

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there. Murodo（むろどう） sits in Tateyama, Toyama — the high point of the Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route（立山黒部アルペンルート）, about two thousand four hundred and fifty metres. Some people call the alpine scenery “Japan’s Switzerland” — that is marketing and mood, not an official place name. The want-to-go plan: first Murodo-daira, then a short walk around みくりが池. Ichinokoshi and Mount Oyama can wait; do not stuff the whole Alpine Route into the same day.

How you get up to Murodo

From the Toyama side you start at 立山駅: the Tateyama Cable Car（鋼索線） takes about seven minutes to Bijodaira, then the Tateyama Highland Bus about fifty minutes to Murodo. Pure riding time is about an hour; queues and transfers are extra. This is not “a ropeway plus a bus” — the aerial ropeway is on the Nagano side, from Kurobedaira to Daikanbo. You can also take the Hokuriku Shinkansen to Toyama, then the Toyama Chiho Railway Tateyama Line to 立山駅; you do not have to drive.

Murodo-daira and みくりが池

室堂 is the terminus and the hub for walks. Rest thirty to sixty minutes after you get off, and drink water — the bus lifts you to over two thousand four hundred metres fast, and altitude sickness (headache, nausea) is real. The short line I want: from 室堂ターミナル to みくりが池, mostly gentle boardwalk and stone, about thirty minutes to an hour return. Toward Jigokudani there are volcanic-gas controls; follow the notices on site. The highland bus can drop you at 彌陀ヶ原 for the wetland.

Season and tickets

The official season is about 15 April to 30 November 2026; the whole stretch closes in winter. Spring into early summer has the “Yuki no Otani” snow wall; the 2026 Festival is about 15 April to 25 June. An adult return from 立山駅 to Murodo is about 7,380 yen (one way about 4,090); follow the official fare table, and buy a WEB ticket first — high season can mean a long wait at the window. Strong wind, heavy rain, and ice can stop the highland bus — check alpen-route.com before you leave.

Do not stuff the day

The want-to-go pace: that day’s goal is the short walk on Murodo-daira. Murodo to Ichinokoshi, then Oyama, is a standard three-and-a-half to four hours return, about five hundred metres of climb — that is another day’s legs; do not bolt it onto a first time up to Murodo. The Tateyama three-peak ridge is more like one or two days. The Nagano-side Kurobe Dam and Ogizawa are the other half of a full crossing; this piece does not schedule them.

The picture I want: the Toyama-side cable car and highland bus, a plateau at two thousand four hundred and fifty metres, みくりが池, the snow wall or autumn colour depending on the season. Fares and opening dates — check the official site again before you leave.

en.title: Inatori Akao: one night, looking at the fishing port and Sagami Bay
en.cardDesc: Not been yet. One night on the bluff, looking at the fishing port and Sagami Bay.
en.html:
Inatori Akao: one night, looking at the fishing port and Sagami Bay

This piece is want-to-go, not been-there. The seed is not rushing sights — it is one night looking at the sea. 稲取赤尾ホテル（いなとりあかおほてる） sits in Inatori, Higashiizu, Shizuoka, on a bluff facing Sagami Bay and the fishing port. The special room / ハンモック (hammock) スイート looks at the port and the sea; a half-open-air bath is in the room. Some people on social media casually call it 「日本一の絶景温泉ホテル」— that is marketing and Instagram talk, not an official ranking. The reason to go is simple: once the bed is booked, there is time to soak and watch the port, without a same-day Tokyo round trip.

How to get there, how the shuttle works

From Tokyo the limited express 「踊り子」 goes straight to 伊豆稲取駅, about two and a half hours. Or take the Shinkansen to Atami, then JR Ito Line into Izukyu; from Atami it is about seventy minutes down. Check-in is about fifteen, check-out about ten — follow the official site.

The station-to-hotel shuttle runs about two to six in the afternoon: after you arrive, call the hotel first (0557-95-2222); the car takes about five minutes. Before two and after six there is no shuttle; you can walk about fifteen minutes, or take a taxi about four to five minutes. In the morning there are fixed departures back to the station (the official site writes nine, nine-thirty, nine-fifty, ten-fifteen, eleven-ten — check again before you leave). Luggage arriving before fourteen cannot be left at the hotel, the FAQ says; the station has coin lockers.

Rooms, baths, how to use the building

The want-to-go choice starts with the room: the top-floor special room, or the ハンモック (hammock) スイート. The window is the fishing port and Sagami Bay; the room has a half-open-air bath, then you can lie there and look at the sea. These rooms are few — specify when you book. If you only book a regular sea-view room, the window still has the sea, but the in-room onsen is an extra outdoor-bath add-on — details on the official FAQ.

To watch the port and the sunset from inside the hotel, book the sixth-floor lookout bath: daytime for the fishing port and Sagami Bay, dusk for the burning clouds toward Amagi. There is also a free 貸切風呂（かしきりぶろ） you can reserve. Day-trip soaking is not offered — to soak you have to stay. Prices and vacancies move fast; check akao-hotel.co.jp before you leave.

Optional half day: the fishing port and こらっしぇ

If the legs are still there, leave half a day to walk to the 稲取漁港／こらっしぇ shop. こらっしぇ sells 金目鯛（キンメダイ） and set-net fish, plus vegetables; the Shizuoka prefecture page says hours are about eight-thirty to fifteen, closed the second Tuesday of each month — confirm on site. Kinme is an Inatori specialty; buying a piece or just looking at the port is enough. Early spring has the 雛のつるし飾り (hanging-doll) season, and autumn susuki on Hosono plateau is often mentioned — look up the town tourism page if that season interests you; this piece does not put them on the same day. Do not stuff 河津七滝 (seven waterfalls), the Kawazu cherry circle, and Hosono plateau into this same night.

The picture I want: calling for the shuttle at 伊豆稲取駅, the port and Sagami Bay from a bluff window, a half-open-air bath or ハンモック in the room, the sixth-floor lookout bath, a fixed-run back to the station the next morning. This is an overnight line, not a same-day round trip. Fares, vacancies, shuttle times — check the official site again before you leave.

en.title: Three powder picks in Japan: Yuzawa, Rusutsu, Furano
en.cardDesc: Want to go. From IG c_lander: Ishiuchi Maruyama, Rusutsu, and Furano.
en.html:
Three powder picks in Japan: Yuzawa, Rusutsu, Furano

This piece is not a record of my own skiing. The source is a recommendation post from the Instagram account c_lander — they wrote they have skied about twenty-five resorts in Japan, and this time picked the three powder spots they like most: steep, fun terrain, high-quality powder, and relatively easy to reach. I only tidied it into a more readable list for planning a holiday later. No day counts; just a list. How you join the trips depends on your leave. Three pins on the map: Ishiuchi Maruyama in Yuzawa, Niigata; Rusutsu in Hokkaido; Furano in Hokkaido.

Yuzawa, Niigata: Ishiuchi Maruyama

石打丸山 sits in Minamiuonuma, Niigata, opened in 1949 — an old large resort near the Kanto suburbs. Many runs, varied terrain; skiers and snowboarders of every level can play. Shinkansen from Tokyo to Echigo-Yuzawa, then a local connection — easier to fit into a short trip than the two Hokkaido spots. The season usually falls between December and April; check opening dates and tickets on the official site before you leave.

Rusutsu, Hokkaido: Rusutsu Resort

留壽都度假村（ルスツリゾート） sits in Rusutsu, Hokkaido — a resort-style compound. Powder and terrain both have a reputation; lodging and food are on site, so you do not have to move to rest. About an hour and a half to two hours from Sapporo or New Chitose; season dates change every year — check the official site before you leave.

Furano, Hokkaido: Furano Ski Resort

富良野滑雪場 sits in Furano, Hokkaido — the town’s representative resort. Varied pitch, steady powder; in winter you can connect from Asahikawa or New Chitose. The bus from New Chitose is about two to two and a half hours; season dates change every year — check the official site before you leave.

Safety

The original post is clear: know your real level, do not go alone; agree the route and the plan with the people you are with before you leave, and watch each other while you ski. Weather and snow on the mountain change fast; judgment matters more than anything.

How other people wrote it

This piece is put together from a post by the Instagram account c_lander — not a record of my own skiing. Places, opening dates, and tickets — check each resort’s official site again before you leave.

The picture I want: the steep runs and old-resort feel of Ishiuchi Maruyama, the one-stop compound at Rusutsu, Furano’s steady powder. Map order: Yuzawa, Niigata → Rusutsu, Hokkaido → Furano, Hokkaido.
